The design-to-code pipeline is modeled as a constrained optimization problem where fidelity to design is maximized subject to token compliance and access control constraints. Each component must satisfy a set of formal invariants: (1) no hardcoded design tokens, (2) full test coverage, (3) server-side access control. Failure modes include token drift, test omission, and client-side-only auth checks. These are mapped to a Bayesian belief network over component states, where evidence from grep, lint, and runtime checks updates posterior probabilities of compliance. The system enforces a dual-layered verification: pre-declaration planning and post-implementation review. The core operators form a lattice of constraints, with design token compliance as the top element and access control as the bottom. Visual regression acts as a proxy for semantic fidelity, while forbidden patterns act as negation clauses in a logical formula defining valid implementations.
